_: ⛔⛔ THE ONE SCHEMA BOTH LANES READ. Added 2026-09-12 because a row satisfied the JS rail and failed the Python one: `vendorTruth.test.js` never read `decision`, so a `decision` written as a STRING passed there and raised AttributeError in `test_vendor_truth.py`. Two rails over one artifact, each with its own idea of the contract, is the second-authority defect this repo keeps paying for — so the contract moved HERE and both rails derive from it. A row now satisfies both lanes or neither.
_how_to_extend: Add the field or hook kind HERE FIRST, then both rails pick it up. A rail that checks something this file does not declare is the drift starting again; each lane has a test asserting it read this file and that the file declares at least the fields that lane enforces.
_decision_is_an_object: ⚠️ NOT a string. It carries `ruled` (the dated decision) and may carry `prior_ruling`, `what_happened`, `owed_to_the_member`, `what_would_reopen_it`, `why_not_accepted_yet`. A string here is the exact shape that passed one lane and crashed the other.
_probe_also_needs: at least one further `under_*` key naming the other convention, so a row states BOTH or neither.

member_hook_kinds.vendorNote: The divergence is about a NAMED TABLE FUNCTION, and a member meets it through `closedTable.json::functions[<name>].vendorNote`. The hook name must be that function name. This is how every row before 2026-09-12 reached a member, and the rails derived the name from `id.split('-')[0]`.
member_hook_kinds.fold: ⭐ ADDED 2026-09-12. The divergence is about a TRANSLATOR-LEVEL fold with no table function to hang a note on — `request.security`, `security`, `tf` and `sym` are none of them table functions. A member meets it through the DISCLOSURE the translation emits on the definition itself. The hook name must be the disclosure channel, e.g. `baseTimeframeFolds`, and some source file must really emit it.

_accepted_owes_a_member: ⛔ A row at status `accepted` must reach a member. With no explicit `member_hook` that is the legacy derivation below (a `vendorNote` on the function `id.split('-')[0]` names); with one, it is the declared kind. `accepted` means the member is TOLD — a row nobody is told about is merely KNOWN, whatever its status field says.
_decision_is_required_only_when: ⚠️ `decision` is required on ACCEPTED rows only — that is where the rails read `decision.ruled`. Measured 2026-09-12: `smoother-seeds-with-sma-of-first-window` carries no `decision` at all and is legitimately at another status, so requiring it everywhere would fail a row nothing is wrong with. A schema stricter than the artifact is a rail that cries wolf.
member_hook_legacy_derivation: ⭐ WHEN A ROW DECLARES NO `member_hook`, the kind is `vendorNote` and the name is `id.split('-')[0]` — the rule every row before 2026-09-12 was written against (`atr-tr-starts-at-bar-1` → `atr`). ⛔ So an explicit hook is needed only when that derivation does NOT name a real table function, which is exactly the translator-level `fold` case. Existing rows keep working untouched; new kinds must say so.
_why_keep_ours: ⚠️ FOUND 2026-09-12, AND IT WAS PYTHON-ONLY. `test_vendor_truth.py` required `decision.why_keep_ours` on every accepted row and the JS rail did not know the field existed — the same split that let a `decision` string through. Declared here so both lanes ask for it. It is the ARGUMENT: why our convention stays, not merely that it was ruled.
_corrected_contract: ⚠⚠ THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SPLIT THIS FILE EXISTS TO END, found 2026-09-12 by the Python lane on a new `corrected` row. `test_vendor_truth.py` required `decision.what_changed` and `correctedIn` on every corrected row; `vendorTruth.test.js` did not know either field existed, so the row passed the JS rail and failed the Python one — the same shape as the `decision`-as-a-string crash and the `why_keep_ours` gap already recorded above. Declared here so both lanes ask. ⛔ `corrected` switches OFF the `vendorNote` obligation, so it owes its own: WHO ruled, WHAT the behaviour is NOW, and WHICH commit or ruling moved it — otherwise it is a door out of the ledger.
_fold_requires_member_note: ⛔ OWNER RULING 2026-09-12. A `fold`-kind hook owed only that SOME SOURCE emitted the channel — which `pine.js` did, on the output row, while no surface rendered it. The channel existed and the member was still never told, which is precisely the state this roster calls 'merely KNOWN'. So an ACCEPTED fold row now owes a `memberNote` on its channel in `closedTable.json::_folds`, both lanes check for it (`parse.js::foldNotesOf`, `api/services/ast_table.py::fold_notes`), and `PineBox` renders it VERBATIM in `pine-vendor-notes` beside the function-level notes. The component composes nothing — one declaration, two readers, one renderer.
